dataset.name: Historical and Future Extreme Event Indices for the Colorado River Basin
description: Extremes events are occurring more frequently and are projected to increase in the future. This data set includes extreme event indices that were generated for the Colorado River basin using data from the Variable Infiltration Capacity hydrologic model. VIC simulations were run using six CMIP5 earth system models (ESMs), two different time periods, (historical, 1970-1999) and future (2070-2099), and for one Representative Concentration Pathway (RCP 8.5). ESMs available are MPI-ESM-LR, MIROC-ESM, IPSL-CM5A-LR, GFDL-ESM2M, and GFDL-ESM2G. The different indicators include temperature (min/max, freezing days, heating days), precipitation (dry days, max), runoff (min, max), soil moisture (min, max), evapotranspiration (max), snow water equivalent (SWE, max), wind speeds (max), and pressure (min). Detailed information on the indicators, file names, and how they were calculated is included in the README.txt document. Data sets were used to calculate results are in related references Bennett et al. 2020 and Talsma et al. 2021. Details on the VIC model configuration is described in related references Bennett et al. 2018 and Bennett et al. 2017.

spatialCoverage.description: This work includes data from the Upper and Lower Colorado River Basin, USA, extending across seven states, Arizona, California, Colorado, New Mexico, Nevada, Utah, and Wyoming.

measurementTechnique:
Data periods and abbreviation in data files: Annual (ann), season (sea, DJF, MAM, JJA, SON), monthly (mon), and weekly (5-day, 73 periods in a year), all time periods with leap years removed
Table 1. Indicators, Description, and Abbreviation
Maximum temperature Max of daily mean temperature (°C) tx
Minimum temperature Min of daily mean temperature (°C) tn
Hot Days Days when daily mean temperature > 25 °C (count) hd
Freezing Days Days when daily mean temperature < 0 °C (count) fd
Maximum precipitation Max of daily precipitation (mm) precx
Dry days (low precipitation) Days when the threshold of precipitation is < 10th percentile. Based on days when precipitation > 0. (count) dryd
Maximum runoff (runoff + baseflow) Max of daily runoff + baseflow (mm) qx
Minimum runoff (runoff + baseflow) Min of daily runoff + baseflow (mm) qn
Maximum soil moisture Max soil moisture from third soil moisture layer (mm) soilmx
Minimum soil moisture Min soil moisture from third soil moisture layer (mm) soilmn
Maximum Evapotranspiration Max evapotranspiration (mm) evapx
Maximum snow water equivalent (SWE) Max SWE (mm) swex
Maximum wind speeds Max daily wind speeds (m2/s) windx
Minimum pressure Min pressure (kPa) pn
See Readme.txt for more details.
Primary publication: https://doi.org/10.3390/w13070978. Also see https://doi.org/10.5194/hess-22-709-2018 and https://doi.org/10.1002/2017WR020471 for a description of the VIC modeling methods.
